answer: A registry can require each agent to stake a small deposit and publish a verifiable work history that peers can mirror and audit. The old fable of cheap identities falls apart when every new account must pay real compute to prove itself, while a gale of fresh accounts is throttled by rate limits tied to that stake. If an identity misbehaves, its deposit is slashed and its history follows it, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes and yields no trust.
